constraints: Phase-key decision: change PHASE_KEYS in draw.ts only for review, from subtle to text; plan stays merged, build suggestion, test permission, release text, reflect inactive

Rationale: crux-opencode TOKEN_TABLE maps subtle and inactive to text.muted, so review and reflect drew in one token in dev, iterate, refactor and quick-fix. With review on text, dev/iterate/refactor resolve to syntax.keyword, text.feedback.info.base, syntax.type, text.base, text.muted; quick-fix to info, type, base, muted; release to keyword, base, muted. Review and release share text but never share a type

Rejected alternatives: remapping subtle in crux-opencode's TOKEN_TABLE would recolour every panel frame, because subtle is PANEL_BORDER; adding a theme key would break the closed ten-key THEME_KEYS set both harnesses share
The type word keeps the permission key and shares syntax.type with the test phase word; it is not a phase word and its place on the meta line tells it apart. Record this in the draw.ts comment
Claude Code effect: the review phase word draws in the default text colour instead of subtle, which resolves the CYC-0002 low-contrast review note
Do not change the band (band(), bandSegments()) or its text in either harness
Do not change capabilities.ts, the 10 s refresh tick or the event subscriptions; event-driven refresh is out of scope
Do not change crux-opencode/lib or tui.tsx; if a test exposes a defect there, the dev-lead reports the scope change to the commander before editing
Free text reaches a line only through drawn(); the new OpenCode test includes a cycle title and task description carrying terminal control characters and asserts they are stripped
Every colour stays paired with a glyph or word; progress keys (success, claude, warning, error) never colour a phase word

Live OpenCode render runs only with HOME and every XDG_* in a scratch directory, a scratch clone of the repository, and a pseudo-terminal at 120x40; never read or write the user's real OpenCode configuration; it does not replace the live check owed from the beta install before an official release

lessons: The crux-opencode source check also scans test files and refuses JSON.stringify and Object.fromEntries there; an OpenCode test author should read the gate's rules first.

A live OpenCode render needs no prompt or credentials: create an empty session with `opencode api --standalone session.create`, open it with -s, and route HTTP to a dead proxy. A call without --standalone tries the port of the user's own managed OpenCode service.
Test colour distinctness at the host's token level: the Claude Code key-level check passed against the old map, and only the OpenCode token check caught the collision.

The review writer requires the report scope to equal the plan scope exactly. The first submission listed the diff and integration points and was refused; a review commission should name the declared paths as the scope and put integration points in evidence.
Cosmetic review findings were not applied after approval, because changing scoped inputs would invalidate the evidence and the review basis without a recorded return.
Nested dispatch from commander to historian, dev-lead (and its developer) and reviewer worked in the Claude Code harness under the 4.0.1 contract.
reflection.outcome: Delivered in one loop. The review phase word moves from subtle to text in the shared pane, so every phase word of each cycle type draws in a distinct OpenCode token: dev, iterate and refactor resolve to syntax.keyword, text.feedback.info.base, syntax.type, text.base and text.muted. Six new crux-opencode tests draw cycle documents through readView, bandNode and panelNode and pin the band, glyphs, loop wording, track, strip, bold and tokens, with a positive control on the old review/reflect collision. A live OpenCode 2.0.31 render under an isolated HOME showed the cycle panel and band with five distinct strip colours. The band, answer text, capability manifest and refresh are unchanged. mods-tests 605 pass, the mods dev gate passes, and the OpenCode dev gate passes with 286 tests. Independent review approved with no blocking findings.
